bricks.headline: UN Climate Summit Ends Without Deal Over Fossil Fuels
bricks.summary: UN climate talks ended without a final deal after two weeks of negotiations. Countries could not agree on whether to cut fossil fuels. European and developing nations rejected a proposed text that left out any mention of fossil fuels.
bricks.whyItMatters: Global climate agreements affect how countries transition to clean energy, which impacts energy prices and weather policies worldwide.
bricks.explainer: Delegates from nearly 200 countries met in Turkey for the annual COP31 UN climate conference. Talks broke down after oil-producing nations opposed rules limiting coal, oil, and gas. A draft agreement was put forward, but representatives from the European Union, the United Kingdom, and developing countries rejected it. They argued that a deal without plans to phase out fossil fuels failed to address rising global temperatures. Because UN climate decisions require consensus, the summit ended without an official agreement.
